subject.title: feat: contextual group activation — LLM-driven peeking/engaged state machine

question: Should OpenClaw support LLM-driven contextual activation for unmentioned group traffic, and if so what core/plugin API, provider-exposure, consent, retention, and logging contract should own it?
rationale: Automation can prove the feature is missing, but cannot choose the privacy boundary, provider exposure, decision-log retention, public config shape, or long-term owner for processing unmentioned group messages.

options.title: Sponsor a default-off design first
options.body: Approve a maintainer-owned design covering consent, provider exposure, retention/logging, config schema, channel coverage, and validation before accepting implementation work.

options.title: Narrow to existing ambient/attention modes
options.body: Pursue timer-based attention windows or documented ambient room-event ergonomics without adding background LLM peeking yet.

options.title: Defer to a plugin/API seam
options.body: Design the observation and decision-hook API needed to keep this optional policy outside core runtime defaults.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a default-off design first
recommendation.body: Approve a maintainer-owned design covering consent, provider exposure, retention/logging, config schema, channel coverage, and validation before accepting implementation work.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history across the central activation and mention-policy code paths that the decision would extend.
